finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the file name is controlled by an attacker, they could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The file name provided by argv[1] is used directly to open a file without any validation or sanitization. The program does not show any handling of the file content that could lead to command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the input words are controlled by an attacker, they could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The input words are directly read from stdin without any validation or sanitization. The program does not show any handling of these inputs that could lead to command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the ladder words are controlled by an attacker, they could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The ladder words are directly printed to stdout without any validation or sanitization. The program does not show any handling of these outputs that could lead to command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the ladder words are controlled by an attacker, they could inject malicious commands.
finding.assumptions: The ladder words are directly pushed into the ladder vector without any validation or sanitization. The program does not show any handling of these inputs that could lead to command execution.
